--api-key.help: require this key from API clients and the dashboard

--backend.help: GPU backend (HIP: experimental gfx1100/gfx1201/gfx1151 on Linux and Windows)

--bench.help: a standard speed test of the installed model (a few minutes, with Maya stopped): decode on three questions and prefill at 2k / 8k tokens; writes maya-bench.txt

--calibrate.help: tune the engine's CPU lane for this PC (the PCIe share and the CPU threads, ~10-15 minutes), then start the model (with --no-start: only tune)

--check.help: only check this PC and exit

--config.help: the installed JSON config to start (its run-maya-<model>.sh does), or for --bench or --report (default: most recently used)

--download-model.help: download the model without asking (the commands and the size are still printed)

--env.help: an engine setting kept in the config, e.g. STRATA_GLM_RAM_HEADROOM_GB=4 (docs/SETTINGS.md)

--gguf-dir.help: use GLM-5.3-Flash GGUF files you already have: the folder with all of them, or the .gguf file (the first one of a split model) when the folder holds several models; it must be writable - the pack is w

--gpu.help: run on this one GPU (CUDA: nvidia-smi; HIP: KFD topology order, on Windows hipInfo's)

--host.help: where the server listens: 127.0.0.1 = this machine only (default), 0.0.0.0 = also other devices on your network (set --api-key too)

--host-compiler.help: the C++ compiler nvcc uses, e.g. g++-12 (when the default g++ is newer than your CUDA accepts)

--llama-dir.help: a llama.cpp checkout at the pinned commit, instead of downloading its source

--models-dir.help: where downloaded models go, each in a folder named after it, e.g. <DIR>/Maya-L/ (default: Maya-data/models next to this folder); use a fast NVMe SSD with ~100 GB free

--no-speed-calibration.help: with --draft dflash2: keep DFlash2 without measuring it against the MTP block

--no-start.help: set up, but do not start the dashboard

--no-vision.help: text only: no image encoder (saves its build and its 1.1 GB of files)

--nvcc.help: the CUDA toolkit's nvcc to build with (default: the newest that fits your GPUs)

--parallel.help: answer up to N requests at once (1-8, default 1), kept in the config: on one GPU they are decoded together, more tokens per second in all; each extra conversation keeps its own context in VRAM, which

--plain.help: the setup in plain text, the answers typed (not on the setup's own screen)

--port.help: the dashboard's and the API's port (default 8080)

--report.help: write maya-report.txt - this PC, the setup and the engine's speed lines - to attach when you report a problem or a speed (nothing is sent anywhere)

--setup.help: set up again instead of starting the installed model

--speed-calibration.help: measure on this PC whether the DFlash2 drafter decodes faster than the MTP block (sustained speed, ~5-20 minutes, the model loaded twice) and keep the faster; then start the model (with --no-start: on

--vram-reserve-mib.help: VRAM in MiB the expert pool leaves free on each GPU for the driver, the desktop and other programs (default 700), kept in the config

--yes.help: take the recommended answers (the model download still needs --download-model)
